decisions.reason: As a recent camera product close to the core portfolio and still presented prominently, it remains a low-carry-cost option in a growing space market despite limited public evidence of commercial traction.
The explicit ESA HERA mission success strongly signals realized value and credibility, so management would very likely retain and support this product.
This sensor suite extends established capabilities into a relevant adjacent field, and with uncertainty still unresolved its option value likely exceeds the cost of keeping it available.

Because it is only mentioned rather than fully featured, this LiDAR offer looks less committed and more expendable, but its fit with miniaturized future spacecraft still argues for keeping it for now.

A newly launched radiation-hard camera sits squarely in the firm’s heritage area, and for such a young product the firm would usually preserve the option until market and mission demand become clearer.

This very new and somewhat niche asteroid-focused camera appears exploratory, yet in a long-cycle space business its uncertainty is still unresolved and the firm is likely to keep the option open another year.
